It did not disappoint, I woke up (face mask still on, whoops!) in NY and my face (not my hair or my clothes) looked like I’d been on a spa holiday. I looked like I’d slept through the whole flight and my skin was dewy for the next two days!The next time I used the mask was just on a normal Sunday during a bath (with Fresh’s lemon bath soaks) and while obviously the bath helped open the pores, I took the mask off and was just amazed at how refreshed my skin felt. Is this what La Mer devouts feel like? Tatcha can do no wrong and even their sheet mask proves it!

Love this cleanser! Skin feels so smooth and clean and keeps my skin from feeling overly dry after cleansing. Skin also appears brighter. I have the full size bottle and it lasted me over a year. I saw this little duo right here and had to have it! Huge fan of this brand!

Love the day cream and face wash. So glad I got the set to try
This is a truly beautiful mask.. It does what it claims..Hydrates and lifts. Face feels amazing

I love the little gold spoon but wish the lid on the night cream had that gold thing on the top like the other creams do to stick the spoon through to make sure I didn’t lose it (Tatcha doesn’t even sell it this way on their website in any formulation for the Indigo series which is weird but whatever I guess).

I am enjoying this serum a lot. It feels and smells extremely luxurious. Plus, It makes my skin feel very soft. But, as far as wrinkles, I think that it takes awhile to start showing any real progress, but it does soften them right away.

Alkyl glucosides used and still technically are considered mild and gentle BUT several years ago were found to actually be allergens that can cause allergic dermatitis reactions. Literally won allergen of the year in 2017. You can google the studies. While a lot of people won’t have reactions many don’t realise that the reason they are breaking out in bumps, redness, little white heads all over is from a reaction to glucosides in products. They are in so many amazing products from all brands and all types of products because it’s still considered genérele and mild but just know that if you are prone to contact dermatitis, have a compromised skin barrier, or sensitive skin in general you should try your best to shy away from glucosides. The most commonly used being decyl glucoside. If you’re one of many that have used Glow recipe and loved the result but not the reaction of breakout you got. Check the list. It’s in the eye cream etc. you might have less of a reaction with rinse offs such as cleansers BUT studies show that you should refrain from even using rinse offs because of worsening future reactions. Hoping this helps people who have had issues with skincare and can’t seem to figure out what the ingredient is. Glucosides come up in search as being safe for sensitive skin until you keep researching. A lot of sunscreens use it as well and it’s not always the uva/uvb ingredient irritating your skin.

I do understand that skincare products generally need 4-6 weeks to see long term benefits, so I will keep trying it. But, in two weeks nothing so far. Ok, now I’ll tell you from the beginning about my experience with this device. 

When I first got this device and began using it, I was so disappointed. I’d followed instruction, I’d shaved before zapping and I’d follow the steps that the booklet told me to do. I did that for several months with no results what so ever.

I then began to use the device more frequently, on the highest setting, for experiment sake. But that yielded no better results neither. I was about to give up when I went back and read the booklet again to double check if I was doing something wrong. And the booklet said that for those with light colored hair, it is recommended to wax or epilate prior to zapping. I don’t have light colored hair but I decided to epilate before zapping anyway, for experiment sake, and that changed everything. 

My hair nearly stopped growing back after that first time. I was shocked. Normally, with shaving, it would grow back within 12 hours, with waxing or epilating, it would grow back within a week or two. I waited a full month and maybe only 30% of the hair came back. 

So, I repeated this process again. Epilate first and zap immediately after. And I do mean immediately afterwards, as in, within seconds… Yes, it sounds very hardcore, it did hurt, but it worked. (But it still hurts a lot less than Tria) For your information, I have never been one with sensitive skin, my skin is actually quite tough, so I knew I could handle this. I definitely can’t speak for everyone. 

When I do this, sometimes I’d literally smell the scent of burning hair, but I didn’t mind it because that was the scent of success, as each time, my hair would grow back slower and less. I went from zapping every two weeks to every month, to every few months. The longer I waited between treatments, the less hair seemed to grow back each time. 

In the end, my Rambutan became a Cherry and I am so happy with the result. I’ve been using this device for over a year now, but I wasted a lot of months, not epilating before zapping. Now, I have so few hair that can pretty count how many there are and that is astonishing to me. 

As far as the cartridge replacement go, I’ve never had to replace it. I’ve never gotten a warning and never had the device stopped working for me and I’m quite impressed with this part.

Another thing too that I wished someone had warned me about is; the flashing…. Girls… It is so bright!! It’s as bright as camera flashes. I cannot look directly at it. I doubt that anyone could. So, I’d recommend putting on some shades to protect your pretty eyes or look away when you zap, that’s what I do.. I hold my breath and I look away.

I have pale skin and dark, coarse hair. It’s all over, but most noticeable on my arms, which have been a source of insecurity since I was about 11. Over the years I tried everything affordable - waxing, hair removal creams, bleaching, etc. Eventually I settled on waxing, in the hopes that after some time, the hair would become finer and less noticeable - with no luck, even after years. tl;dr - it worked on light skin/dark coarse hair very, very well. Thrilled with results, would recommend.

There seems to be a 0% reduction, but the hair is finer.

Bottom line, I think this is worth it if the hair you want to treat is fine and dark (not gray or blond). Be prepared to invest A LOT of time on zapping.

A Little about my skin and hair dilemmas. I am very light skinned around the tone of NC 20, NARS SG Fuji, Koh Gen do 113. My hair is extremely thick and course in the color of dark espresso to black. My hair grows extremely quick and I would have no choice but to shave my legs and under arms daily and even then by the afternoon my legs would start to feel prickly  Too bad I couldn’t bottle whatever made my hair grow so quickly, I would have made millions! Now on to this long winded review.So I have currently owned this device a little longer than 2 months now and have completed all the recommended 7 treatments. I wanted to wait so that I may give full review because 445$ is quite the investment for a lot of us. So the big question is does it work? And you will not like my answer because it depends… If you’re expecting to receive COMPLETELY hair free (think the Sphnx cat baldness) including all peach fuzz eradicated, it’s just not going to happen. BUT if you do have realistic expectations I hope you will not be disappointed. What I mean by realistic is 50-98% per area of hair reduction. I say per area because I have done my entire body, face, underarms, arms, bikini, and legs. Each area, even though treatment was all performed in the same manner at the same time, reacted a little differently. Let’s start from the face. I have mostly peach fuss on my face that is barely noticeable and does not bother me but what did were the small dark hairs that I would have to wax/pluck from the sides of my moth as well as 4 dark hairs that would come up on my chin. After 7 treatments the peach fuzz had only a little reaction while the 4 hairs on my chin I have not seen treatment 2!! As far as the hairs on the corner of my mouth they are drastically reduced by up to 80 %( That is 80% has not regrown at all!) I would rate this a negative 10 if a could for the lack of research and the inexperience/incompetence of the person(s) who formulated this product. I did not see any results. No brightening, increases smoothness, nothing, and here’s why that is to be expected: this product contains both ascorbic acid (vitamin c) and glycolic acid, both are great to include in your skincare routine but they need to be used SEPARATELY! Although it is safe to combine them, they are substantially less EFFECTIVE TOGETHER! When combined the pH of the acids is changed reducing their effectiveness.
